plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: A long-lived herbaceous perennial with large, fragrant, often double blooms atop sturdy stems with glossy, deeply lobed leaves. A cornerstone of cottage gardens and cut flower production.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (May to June in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to Siberia, Mongolia, and northern China; widely cultivated in temperate gardens across North America and Europe
plants.funFact: Peonies can live and bloom for over 50 years in the same spot, and in China they have been cultivated for more than 1,500 years as symbols of prosperity and honor.

plants.name: Iris germanica
plants.description: A rhizomatous perennial with sword-shaped gray-green leaves and showy flowers with three upright standards and three drooping falls, the latter bearing a fuzzy 'beard'.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring (May in temperate Northern Hemisphere regions)
plants.location: Hybrid of Mediterranean origin; cultivated throughout temperate regions worldwide
plants.funFact: The iris is named after the Greek goddess of the rainbow, and the dried rhizomes of related species, called orris root, are used in perfumery.

plants.name: Rosa canina
plants.description: A vigorous, arching, thorny deciduous shrub of hedgerows and woodland edges, bearing delicate five-petaled flowers followed by bright red rose hips in autumn.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late May through July in Europe
plants.location: Native to Europe, northwest Africa, and western Asia; naturalized in North America, Australia, and New Zealand
plants.funFact: Rose hips from the dog rose are extremely rich in vitamin C, and during World War II British children collected them to make a vitamin-rich syrup.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A graceful tropical to subtropical tree with fern-like leaves that erupts in clouds of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers, carpeting the ground beneath when they fall.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring in the Northern Hemisphere subtropics (May to June); October to November in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to South America; planted in Mexico, Southern California, Florida, Africa, and Australia
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, so many jacarandas have been planted that it is nicknamed the 'Jacaranda City', and in Mexico City the late spring bloom turns streets purple.
